==English==
{{wp}}
[[File:Hexahedron.svg|thumb|A cube]]

===Etymology 1===
From {{uder|en|fro|cube|}}, from {{uder|en|la|cubus}}, from {{uder|en|grc|κύβος|}}.

{{displaced|ang|tæfel}} ("cube, die, game with dice or tables").

====Pronunciation====
* {{enPR|kyo͞ob|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/kjuːb/}}
* {{enPR|kyo͞ob|a=US}}, {{IPA|en|/kjub/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-cube.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|uːb|s=1}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|geometry}} A [[regular]] [[polyhedron]] having six identical square faces.
#: {{ux|en|When the math teacher is teaching the class about '''cubes''', he asks them to imagine a cardboard box whose width, length, and height are all the same.}}
# Any object more or less in the form of a cube.
#: {{hypo|en|sugar cube|stock cube}}
#: {{ux|en|A: One '''cube''' or two? B: Oh, no sugar for me, thanks.}}
# {{senseid|en|Q861555}} {{lb|en|mathematics}} The third [[power]] of a [[number]], [[value]], [[term]] or expression.
#: {{ant|en|cube root<id:Q1774143>}}
#: {{ux|en|The '''cube''' of 2 is 8.}}
#: {{ux|en|The '''cube''' of 0.5 is 0.125.}}
# {{lb|en|computing}} A [[data structure]] consisting of a [[three-dimensional]] [[array]]; a [[data cube]].
# A {{w|Rubik's cube}} style puzzle, not necessarily in the shape of a cube.
# {{senseid|en|Q2140397}} {{lb|en|informal|automotive}} {{clipping of|en|cubic inch<id:Q2140397><alt:cubic inch(es)>}}.
#: {{ux|en|As if the 383 weren't already a roaring beast, in 1972 they bored it out some more, bringing it up to 400 '''cubes'''. This 400-'''cube''' monster could launch a land yacht like the Plymouth Fury from zero to sixty in under ten seconds.}}
# {{senseid|en|uncool person}} {{lb|en|1950s|_|slang|dated}} An extremely socially [[conventional]] or [[conservative]] person, more so than even a [[square]].

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive|arithmetic}} To raise to the third power; to determine the result of multiplying by itself twice.
#: {{ux|en|Three '''cubed''' can be written as 3<sup>3</sup>, and equals twenty-seven.}}
#* {{RQ:Beckett Watt|text=From this severe trial Mr. Nackybal emerged with distinction, having in his '''cubing''' made only twenty-five slight mistakes out of the forty-six cubes demanded, and in his rooting, out of the fifty-three extractions propounded, committed a mere matter of four trifling errors!}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To form into the shape of a cube.
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To cut into cubes.
#: {{syn|en|dice}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Cube''' the ham right after adding the curry to the rice.}}
# {{sid|en|Rubik's cube}} {{lb|en|intransitive}} To use a [[Rubik's cube]].
#: {{ux|en|He likes to '''cube''' now and then.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|author=Yu-chen Li|quotee=Lin Yangxi|title=Specialist coaches and hours of practice a day: the making of China’s six-year-old Rubik’s Cube prodigy|date=2026-09-26|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/26/dream-come-true-six-year-old-rubiks-cube-world-record|author2=Amy Hawkins|passage=“She has gained a lot of love and attention through '''cubing'''.”|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261018142511/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/26/dream-come-true-six-year-old-rubiks-cube-world-record|archivedate=18 October 2026}}

The box, about six inches '''cube''', contained slots to take four cut-out scenes, the front of the box had another cut-out, and the back was painted with a landscape, making six 'curtains' in all.}}

===Etymology 2===
Clipped form of {{m|en|cubicle}} (with intentional reference to their common shape per [[#Etymology 1|''cube'', etymology 1]]), which from {{uder|en|la|cubiculum||a small bedchamber or lounge}}, from {{m|la|cubare||to lie down}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# A [[cubicle]], especially one of those found in offices.
#: {{ux|en|My co-worker annoys me by throwing things over the walls of my '''cube'''.}}
